story_title: Lina and Adams and the Lunchbox Day
lesson: Learn lunch food words in English!
title: Lina and Adams and the Lunchbox Day 🥪 | Learn Food Words in English for Kids | Moon Tales Kids
description:
Today the class eats lunch in the park! Lina and Adams pack their lunchboxes, and when Adams drops his sandwich, Lina kindly shares. 🥪🧃🍎
In this English story for kids, children learn 8 new words: lunchbox, bread, cheese, egg, juice, water, crunchy and napkin. Listen, repeat, and learn English with Lina, Adams and Milo the cat.

📚 New words in this story:
🍱 lunchbox — علبة الغداء — la boîte à goûter
🍞 bread — خبز — le pain
🧀 cheese — جبن / فرماج — le fromage
🥚 egg — بيضة — l'œuf
🧃 juice — عصير — le jus
💧 water — ماء / الما — l'eau
🥕 crunchy — مقرمش — croquant
🧻 napkin — منديل / كلينيكس — la serviette

👨‍👩‍👧 For parents: pack a lunchbox with your child and name each food in English. Talk about sharing with friends. Pause after each new word and say it out loud. Perfect for ages 3 to 8 and for children learning English as a second language.

🇲🇦 قصة باللغة الإنجليزية للأطفال لتعلم أسماء الأكل والمشاركة مع الأصدقاء.
🇫🇷 Une histoire en anglais pour enfants pour apprendre les mots du déjeuner et le partage.

lines.text: Good morning! The sun is shining in the kitchen.
Adams! Today our class will eat lunch in the park!
Hooray! We need to pack our lunch.
Mama gives Lina and Adams two little boxes. One is pink, and one is blue.
A lunchbox is a box to carry our food to school.
Say it with me: lunchbox!
Meow! Is there food for me?
First, they need bread for a sandwich.
Here is the bread. It is soft and brown.
Two pieces of bread for me, and two for you.
Bread is a food made from flour. We eat it every day.
Can you say it? Bread!
Milo sniffs the bread. Sniff, sniff!
Sorry, Milo. This bread is for our sandwich.
Next, Adams opens the fridge.
Look! Yellow cheese! I love cheese!
Lina puts the cheese on the bread. Then she closes the sandwich.
Ta-da! A cheese sandwich!
Cheese is a food made from milk.
Say it with me: cheese!
Say cheese! Ha ha! Smile, Lina!
Mama gives them an egg. It is cooked, so it is hard inside.
Only grown-ups use the hot stove. Mama cooked the egg this morning.
Can I take the shell off?
Adams taps the egg gently. Tap, tap, tap. The shell comes off.
An egg comes from a chicken. It is white outside and yellow inside.
Let's say it together: egg!
One egg for each lunchbox.
Now they want something to drink.
Can we take orange juice, Mama?
Mama pours orange juice into two little bottles.
Orange juice is sweet and yummy!
Juice is a drink made from fruit.
Can you say it? Juice!
We will drink our juice at the park.
Mama gives them a bottle of water too.
Milo is drinking from his bowl. Lap, lap, lap!
Look! Milo is drinking water.
Water is the best drink when we are thirsty.
We drink water every day to grow strong and healthy.
Say it with me: water!
Meow! I love water too!
At school, the teacher writes on the board.
It says: Lunch at the park!
I have my lunchbox. Do you have your lunchbox, Adams?
Yes! It is in my hand.
Everybody walks to the park together, holding hands.
Stop, look and listen at the street. Then they cross safely.
The park! I can see the trees!
At the park, they sit on the green grass.
Lina has an apple. Adams has a carrot.
Lina bites her apple. Crunch, crunch!
My carrot is crunchy too! Crunch!
Crunchy food makes a loud sound when we bite it.
Can you say it? Crunchy!
Crunchy apples are my favourite!
Now it is time for the sandwiches.
Adams opens his lunchbox. But oh no! His sandwich falls on the grass.
Oh no! My sandwich is dirty. I cannot eat it now.
Adams feels sad. His tummy is still hungry.
A little bird hops near the sandwich. Tweet, tweet!
Don't be sad, Adams. I have an idea!
Lina breaks her cheese sandwich into two pieces.
Here, Adams. Half for you, and half for me.
Really? Thank you, Lina! You are so kind.
Sharing is kind. Sharing makes friends happy.
Here, Lina. You can have some of my egg.
Now they both have a sandwich and an egg.
Sharing is fun!
After lunch, their hands are a little bit sticky.
I have a napkin. Let's clean our hands and mouths.
Wipe, wipe! Now their hands are clean.
A napkin is a soft paper we use to clean our hands and mouths when we eat.
Say it with me: napkin!
And we put the rubbish in the bin. The park stays clean!
In the evening, Lina and Adams are back home.
Meow! Meow! You are back!
Mama, I dropped my sandwich, but Lina shared her lunch with me.
Mama smiles. She is proud of Lina.
Tomorrow, let's pack a lunchbox together again!
And a little treat for Milo too!
Lunchbox, bread, cheese, egg, juice, water, crunchy and napkin. What a yummy day!
